narrative:
The model estimated a 34% chance that you would represent a bad credit risk. For this lending decision, that estimated risk was above the bank’s acceptable level, so your application was denied. The most influential factor was your credit history, recorded as critical/other credits. In this assessment, that factor worked in your favour and reduced the assessed risk. However, the next two most important factors pushed the decision toward bad credit. Your checking account status showed a balance of 0-200 DM, which increased the risk; among approved applicants, no recorded checking account was much more common (59.2%) than this balance range (18.4%). The amount you requested, 8,386 DM, was also a risk-increasing factor and was far above the average approved request of about 3,020 DM. Together, these two risk signals outweighed the favourable credit-history signal.

To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a smaller loan or providing a guarantor or collateral, and work on strengthening your checking account balance and payment record. Ask the bank whether any credit-history information can be corrected or explained, and reapply when your requested amount is closer to what the bank typically approves relative to your financial profile.
